newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian wheat prices to ease, says minister.
newsitem.headline: Indian wheat prices to ease, says minister.

text.p: India's domestic wheat prices are expected to fall following the arrival of imported wheat, Food Minister Devendra Prasad Yadav said on Friday.

About 600,000 tonnes of imported wheat had already arrived and another 600,000 tonnes was expected to arrive by the end of March, the Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Yadav as telling reporters in the western city of Ahmedabad.

In December, the federal government authorised the state-run State Trading Corporation (STC) to import up to two million tonnes of wheat in 1996/97 (April-March) to augment supplies and check rising domestic prices.
Senior STC officials earlier said it had already contracted to import 1.47 million tonnes of wheat.
"For the first time the imports have been made without any middle-men and it was a government to government deal. Wheat will be available at 6,400 rupees per tonne," Yadav was quoted as saying.
Wheat is currently 6,700 rupees per tonne in the domestic markets. Yadav said prices had shot up as traders had hoarded stocks to sell it in the lean season.
"It was a calculated move by speculators who diverted money from the sluggish stock markets for hoarding wheat as they knew about the shortfall in wheat production this year," Yadav said.
India's wheat output fell to 62.6 million tonnes in the 1995/96 crop year from 65.47 million in 1994/95. India has set a target of 66 million tonnes for the 1996/97 (July/June) crop year.
